transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-11-08 16:00 UTC; Duration: 47m; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jason Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Crownline Head of AI), Tom Becker (Infra), Leo Park (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick discovery. Customer prefers PLG first but has enterprise constraints.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Jason will be the SE on the call. Quick go-around?
00:08 Aisha (Crownline): Hi all, Aisha here, leading ML at Crownline. We're evaluating ways to add a product chat assistant across web and in-store kiosks. Main asks: latency, cost, and data residency.
00:18 Tom (Crownline): Tom, infra. I care about network, VPC, and encryption keys.
00:22 Leo (Crownline): Leo, product. Focused on time-to-first-token and quick experiment flow for the PMs.
00:27 Maya (Redwood): Great. At a high-level Redwood offers hosted API with free credits to get to first token quickly, then dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private for full isolation. Today let's map that to your constraints.
00:43 Jason (Redwood): Quick question on traffic shape — what peaks look like and token lengths?
00:49 Aisha: Typical prods will be 200–800 token exchanges; primarly 512 avg maybe. Peak concurrency around 80–150 concurrent sessions, ballpark 100 req/s when promotions run.
01:05 Jason: OK so 100 req/s with ~512 tokens is useful for sizing. For hosted quickstart we can give credits for canonical workload and you can measure p95 latencies.
01:18 Tom: For hosted, how do we handle PII? We can't send raw payment or PII outside our VPC for compliance.
01:26 Maya: Totally. We see two patterns: 1) start with hosted but sanitize or token-filter PII; 2) start with dedicated or private if raw data must never leave your network. We can provide private deployment with VPC peering and KMS so keys stay on your side.
01:43 Aisha: Would PLG/self-serve hosted be locked down enough for us to prototype? Our security team wants SOC2 and audit logs.
01:50 Maya: Our hosted has SOC2 compliance and audit logs; we can share the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram. If they still need, we can move to Dedicated next — dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and private networking controls, but it's a commitment.
02:05 Leo: What is typical time-to-first-token if we go the PLG route with free credits? Say we sign up today.
02:12 Jason: TL;DR: sign up, create API key, run a sample request — we aim for minutes. With our quickstart template most teams hit first token within 15–30 minutes including onboarding.
02:24 Aisha: That sounds optimistic; any gotchas?
02:27 Maya: Common gotcha is billing/organization setup and SSO for enterprise. For a single team self-serve it's fast. For enterprise SSO and procurement it slows to days/weeks.
02:38 Tom: How does caching and batching work? We have repeated prefix prompts for the chat system.
02:44 Jason: We have auto KV cache and prefix caching; note transcription sometimes says KV cash, haha. It helps reduce token cost for repeated prompts. We can configure batching to keep latency low while improving throughput.
03:02 Aisha: On latency: we need p95 <200ms for interactive feel on web. Is that realistic with hosted?
03:09 Jason: For our smaller models on hosted, yes in many regions. It depends on model choice and sequence length. For p95 under 200ms you may need to pick a lower-latency model or use dedicated reserved capacity to pin GPUs and avoid noisy neighbor effects.
03:25 Tom: Cost signal — any ballpark numbers for 512 tokens?
03:30 Maya: We'll send a reference cost sheet but rough rule: hosted per-token pricing varies by model complexity; dedicated reduces per-token cost via bulk committed capacity and quantization recommendations. We'll include model/quantization playbook in the follow-up.
03:45 Leo: What about private deployment? If we need on-prem because of data residency, how fast can that be stood up?
03:52 Jason: Private on-prem is more involved. Typical timeline is weeks to months depending on infra readiness and approvals. There's a pre-packaged on-prem path for air-gapped but it's the longest route.
04:06 Aisha: So our fall plan could be: 1) immediate PLG test with hosted free credits to validate UX and measures; 2) dedicated pilot for predictable perf if costs align; 3) private if compliance forces it. Does that map to Redwood?
04:19 Maya: Exactly. Many customers follow that staircase.
04:22 Tom: In terms of security, can you map the keys and encryption model? We need KMS integration and customer-managed keys for the dedicated/private offering.
04:31 Jason: Yes. Dedicated and private both support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit; for customer-managed KMS we move to dedicated/private.
04:43 Aisha: What about SSO? Our enterprise SAML is required before we give API keys broadly.
04:48 Maya: We support SAML SSO for enterprise accounts. For PLG quickstart you can create a normal API key and later upgrade under the same org to SSO.
04:58 Leo: Benchmarks — can Redwood run a quick test to show 100 req/s at target latency?
05:03 Jason: Yes, Jason: we can run a 1-2 hour benchmark with your sample traffic pattern; we often run a smoke test on hosted, and for dedicated we can provision a pilot cluster. We'll propose a plan.
05:18 Maya: Do you have a decision timeline?
05:20 Aisha: We'd like to launch a small pilot by end of November and a product experiment in December. Procurement wants initial cost numbers and the security pack.
05:31 Maya: We'll aim to get the SOC2/security docs and rough pilot pricing over in two business days. We'll also send the quickstart link and a pre-populated Postman collection you can share with PMs.
05:43 Tom: On networking — for dedicated pilot, do you support VPC peering or private link?
05:49 Jason: We support VPC peering and private link patterns depending on cloud. We'll include network diagrams for each deployment type.
05:58 Aisha: Anything else we should discuss now?
06:00 Leo: A small point — can we limit model exports or caching so we don't persist user utterances past 30 days? Data retention policies?
06:08 Maya: Yes we have retention controls; we'll share default retention and options to configure shorter retention or log redaction.
06:16 Aisha: Great.
06:20 Maya: Okay quick recap: Redwood to share SOC2, security brief, network diagrams, and a pilot benchmark plan. Crownline to share sample traffic and PII inventory. Follow-up meeting to scope dedicated pilot week of 11/16.
06:37 Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
06:40 End of recording.
